title: Kubernetes Secret Mounted in Default Namespace

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay or inject sample `kube:audit` events matching `*` into `index=kube`. Confirm UC-4.9.18 search returns >=1 row and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `kube:audit` traffic without `*` markers. Confirm the search returns zero rows and alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=kube` sourcetype=`kube:audit` collected via Splunk Connect for Kubernetes; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit"
| table _time user.username verb objectRef.resource objectRef.name
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.9.18_kubernetes_secret_mounte_18"
| sort -_time
description: Monitors `kube:audit` telemetry to detect kubernetes secret mounted in default namespace. Identifies anomalous or high-risk activity for security and operations review.
value: Default namespace secrets often lack governance. Detecting kubernetes secret mounted in default namespace early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=kube sourcetype=kube:audit.
visualization: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report.
knownFalsePositives: Approved change windows; documented automation service principals; sandbox accounts excluded via lookup.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=kube`.
• Install and configure Splunk Connect for Kubernetes with the modular input for `kube:audit`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.9.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `user.username` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=kube sourcetype=kube:audit.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=kube sourcetype="kube:audit"
| table _time user.username verb objectRef.resource objectRef.name
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.9.18_kubernetes_secret_mounte_18"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `kube:audit` in `index=kube` to detect kubernetes secret mounted in default namespace. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Kubernetes audit dashboard for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `user.username` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_9_18_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Splunk Connect for Kubernetes and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of kubernetes secret mounted in default namespace so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
